rules.typeAdvice: Move numericFormat.culture to locale by hand if this column is numeric, and delete it if it is not. The tool kept it because it found no type: 'numeric' here or in the settings above. numericFormat does nothing in a column of another type, but 18.0 reads locale for text sorting, filtering, and search, and for date and time columns, so a moved culture would change how this column behaves.
rules.levelAdvice: Set locale on the numeric columns that used numericFormat.culture, or on the grid if every column should use it, then delete culture. The tool kept numericFormat.culture here because a grid-level locale reaches every other column too: date, time, intl-date, intl-time, and intl-datetime columns format with it, and text sorting, filtering, and search lower-case with it.
rules.report: Check the numbers this column shows. With a culture and no pattern, 17.1 formatted them with the Numbro pattern '0': every decimal and no grouping, so 1234.56 showed as 1234,56 for de-DE. In 18.0 the object goes to Intl.NumberFormat, which groups the digits and keeps three decimals unless the options say otherwise: 1.234,56 for de-DE, and 1234.5678 becomes 1.234,568. Add useGrouping: false and maximumFractionDigits: 20 to numericFormat to keep the 17.1 output.
rules.readerAdvice: Move numericFormat.culture to locale and update the code that reads it in the same change. A custom renderer, editor, or validator may read numericFormat.culture, but 18.0 formats with locale, so that code would fall back to its default culture if only the key moved.

rules.name: correctFormat
rules.readerAdvice: The built-in cell types ignore correctFormat in 18.0, but a custom validator, editor, or renderer can still read it, so delete it only when no such code does.
rules.advice: Use valueParser or valueSetter to correct entered values. 18.0 removed correctFormat. The date, time, intl-date, and intl-time cell types work with ISO 8601 values and do not reformat input.

rules.name: datePickerConfig
rules.readerAdvice: The built-in date cell types ignore datePickerConfig in 18.0, but a custom editor (a Pikaday or Moment.js recipe) reads it from the cell properties, so delete it only when no such code does.
rules.advice: Check the native date input, which replaces Pikaday. The date and intl-date cell types use it, and 18.0 removed datePickerConfig.

rules.message: Rename columnHeaders to colHeaders: the export option is deprecated since 17.1 and 19.0 removes it. colHeaders keeps the meaning of the value.
